subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should OpenClaw fix this as a shared proxy transport bug covering explicit and environment SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS routes, or narrow the supported Telegram proxy contract first?
rationale: The report is plausible and in scope, but the remaining fix direction changes compatibility-sensitive proxy behavior and needs live Telegram SOCKS evidence before automation should create another repair branch.

options.title: Repair Shared Proxy Handling
options.body: Treat the open SOCKS proxy PR as a candidate, but require scheme-aware explicit/env proxy coverage, regression tests, and live Telegram SOCKS proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Define Supported Proxy Contract
options.body: Document the supported Telegram proxy schemes and close or redirect configurations outside that contract only after maintainers make the policy explicit.

options.title: Request Fresh Diagnostics First
options.body: Ask the reporter for a current-main service-context run with redacted Telegram network logs before choosing between proxy-scheme and DNS/IPv4 fixes.

recommendation.title: Repair Shared Proxy Handling
recommendation.body: Treat the open SOCKS proxy PR as a candidate, but require scheme-aware explicit/env proxy coverage, regression tests, and live Telegram SOCKS proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent ownership of the shared Undici proxy helper and related Telegram transport review surface.
